Rashi on Ketubot 38b:10:1.hebrew: יש בגר בקבר - אם מתה בנערותה עד שלא עמדה בדין, והגיע זמן בגרותה בקבר, מי חשיב בגר או לא? ולקמיה מפרש ואזיל למאי הלכתא:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:10:1.english: Is there grown-woman status in the grave - If she died while a young woman before she stood trial, and the time of her grown-woman status arrived [while she was] in the grave, is it considered grown-woman status or not? And further on, [the Gemara] proceeds to explain for what halakhic [difference this matters].

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:10:2.hebrew: יש בגר בקבר - וכי היכי דאם לא הספיקה לעמוד בדין עד שבגרה, תנן לקמן בפרק נערה שנתפתתה (כתובות דף מא:) דהרי הן לעצמה ולא לאביה, והשתא נמי, בגר בקבר מפקיע כח האב, ובנה ירית לה אם יש לה בן:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:10:2.english: Is there grown-woman status in the grave - Just as, if she did not manage to stand in court before she reached grown-woman status, we learn later in the chapter Na'arah Shenitpatah (Ketubot 41b) that [the fine payments] belong to her and not to her father — so too now, grown-woman status in the grave nullifies the father's right, and her son inherits it, if she has a son.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:1:1.hebrew: אימא בתולה לגזירה שוה - ולאו למעוטי בעולה, ויהא קנס לבעולה:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:1:1.english: Say [that] “virgin” [is] for a verbal analogy - And not to exclude a non-virgin, and [thus] there would be a fine for a non-virgin.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:1.hebrew: מסתברא אשר לא אורסה לגזירה שוה - ואפי' אורסה, אית לה קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:1.english: It stands to reason [that] “Who was not betrothed” [is used] for a verbal analogy - And even [if] she was betrothed, she is entitled to the fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:2.hebrew: שהרי אני קורא בה נערה בתולה - אע"פ שנתארסה ונתגרשה, דהא נערה בתולה היא כדכתיב קרא. אבל בעולה, שאין אני קורא בה נערה בתולה, אין לה קנס:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:2.english: As I [can] read “a young woman, a virgin” regarding her - Even though she was betrothed and divorced, for she is [indeed] a young woman [and] a virgin, as the verse writes. However, a non-virgin, regarding whom I cannot read “a young woman, a virgin,” has no fine.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:3.hebrew: אדרבה בתולה לגזירה שוה - ולאו למעוטי בעולה בזנות, אלא יש לה קנס לבעולה בזנות, שהרי אני קורא אותה נערה אשר לא אורסה:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:3.english: On the contrary, [the word] “virgin” [is used] for the verbal analogy - And not to exclude a woman who had intercourse licentiously; rather, a woman who had intercourse licentiously is entitled to the fine, since I [can] call her “a young woman who was not betrothed.”

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:4.hebrew: מסתברא - ארוסה יש לה קנס, ובעולה אין לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:4.english: It stands to reason - A betrothed [woman] has [a] fine, and a non-virgin does not.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:5.english: For this one's body has changed - and her degradation is not so great.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:2:6.english: And this [woman] - who was betrothed and divorced, her body did not change.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:3:1.hebrew: הא סברא - דחמשים כסף דאונס שקלים הן, וכסף ישקול דמפתה יהו חמשים:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:3:1.english: This reasoning - that the fifty [pieces of] silver of a rapist are shekels, and [the phrase] “he shall weigh money” of a seducer shall be fifty.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:3:2.hebrew: כמוהר הבתולות - מנין המפורש אצל אונס, דהיינו חמשים:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:3:2.english: Like the dowry of the virgins - The number specified regarding rape, that is, fifty.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:3:3.english: And the dowry of the virgins - [They] shall be shekels.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:3:4.english: Like this - For it is written regarding it, "he shall weigh" [meaning shekels].

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:4:1.english: There is a difficulty [with the statement] of Rabbi Akiva - [namely, that] of the baraita, where he said her fine [goes] to her father.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:4:2.english: Against [the statement of] Rabbi Akiva - [that] of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:5:1.hebrew: לא אתיא גזירה שוה ומפקא לקרא מפשטיה לגמרי - דאתא פשטיה לאשמועינן הא ארוסה לעצמה, וחד מתרוייהו לאפנויי; אי נמי לא מופני, ליכא למיפרך מידי:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:5:1.english: A verbal analogy does not come and divert the verse from its plain meaning entirely - For its plain meaning comes to teach us [that] a betrothed woman [receives the fine] for herself, and one of the two [verses is left] free [for the verbal analogy]; or even if [neither] is free, there is nothing to refute.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:5:2.hebrew: אלא לרבי עקיבא דברייתא וכי אתיא גזירה שוה ומפקא מפשטיה לגמרי - דלא דריש פשטא דאשר לא אורסה כלל, ומשוי אורסה כלא אורסה, ואם כן מיעקר משמעותיה:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:5:2.english: However, according to Rabbi Akiva of the baraita, does a verbal analogy come and divert [the verse] from its plain meaning entirely? - For he does not expound the plain meaning of "who was not betrothed" at all, and he equates a betrothed [woman] with one who is not betrothed, and if so, its meaning is uprooted.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:6:1.hebrew: קרי ביה - בפשטיה, "אשר לא ארוסה", למעוטי ארוסה:
Rashi on Ketubot 38b:6:1.english: Read it - According to its plain meaning, "who is not betrothed," to exclude a betrothed [young woman].

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:6:2.english: [She] is [subject to] stoning - And from [the verse] "and there be no fatality" [Exodus 21:22], exemption from payment is derived.

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:8:1.english: To whom [is] her fine - [The Gemara] assumes [it] is referring to an ordinary raped [woman].

Rashi on Ketubot 38b:9:1.english: [If] one had intercourse with her and she died - The father did not manage to bring him to court before she died.

Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:10:1.hebrew: יש בגר בקבר ודבנה הוי - וא"ת: היכי מצי למימר שתהא מורשת קנס לבנה? הא אין אדם מוריש קנס לבניו, כדאמרינן ריש פרק נערה לקמן (כתובות דף מב:)! ובסמוך נמי אמר: "יש בגר בקבר ופקע אב", ואי אדם מוריש קנס, כי יש בגר בקבר נמי לא פקע אב ויהא לו מתורת ירושה. ומיהו ההיא דבסמוך יש לדחות, דנפקא מינה אם היא חייבת לאחרים — דאם יש בגר בקבר פקע אב, אע"ג דאדם מוריש קנס, דנוטלין בעלי חובות; אבל אם אין בגר בקבר, אין נוטלין בעלי חובות כלום, דלא פקע אב והקנס הוא שלו ולא שלה. ויש לומר דהכא ה"מ לאקשויי: והא אין מורשת קנס לבנה! אלא דעדיפא מיניה פריך. ור"י מוקי הך בעיא דהכא בבושת ופגם, דממונא הוי ויכולה להוריש. ואע"ג דתנן בריש נערה (כתובות מא:): "לספיקה לעמוד בדין עד שמת האב — הרי הן של עצמה", ואבושת ופגם נמי קאי, מדקתני "הרי הן" משמע דאין יכול להוריש בושת ופגם! ואור"י דלענין זה ודאי איתקוש בושת ופגם לקנס, דכתיב: "תחת אשר ענה", מכלל דאיכא בושת ופגם — דלמי שזה ניתן, זה ניתן; אבל למילי אחריני לא איתקוש, דהא בושת ופגם משלם ע"פ עצמו, וקנס אינו משלם ע"פ עצמו. אבל הקשה ריב"ם: דאמרינן במרובה (ב"ק דף עא: ושם): א"ל: "חמשה בקר" אמר רחמנא, ולא חמשה חצאי בקר. איתיביה: "גנב משל אביו וטבח ומכר, ואח"כ מת אביו — משלם תשלומי ד' וה'". והא הכא כיון דמת אביו, זכה ליה במנתא דידיה, וקתני דמשלם תשלומי ד' וה'! ומשני: הב"ע שעמד בדין. משמע דאי לאו משום ד"חמשה בקר" ולא חמשה חצאי בקר, הוה אתי ליה שפיר ולא הוה צריך לאוקומי בשעמד בדין; אלמא דאדם מוריש קנס לבניו! ומיהו יש לדחות דה"מ למימר "וליטעמיך". אבל קשה דמסיק: לצפרא א"ל: "חמשה בקר" אמר רחמנא, ואפי' חמשה חצאי בקר. א"ל: מאי שנא רישא ומאי שנא סיפא? פירוש: דקתני "גנב משל אביו ומת ואח"כ טבח ומכר — פטור". א"ל: רישא קרינן ביה "וטבחו" כולו באיסורא, סיפא לא קרינן "וטבחו" כולו באיסורא. משמע דאי קרינן ביה "וטבחו" כולו באיסורא חייב, אע"ג דלא עמד בדין, דאדם מוריש קנס לבניו — דאי בעמד בדין, לא מחייב קנס, דשלו הוא טובח ומוכר! ותי' ר"י דמיירי דעמד בדין ואמרו: "חייב אתה ליתן לו", דאם הוא טובח אחרי כן חייב, כדאמרינן בהגוזל (שם דף קו: ושם). ור"י הלבן תירץ דההיא דפרק נערה איירי לענין קרבן שבועה. והכי פירושו דסוגיא דהתם: מודינא לך לענין קרבן שבועה, דרחמנא פטריה מ"וכחש בעמיתו בפקדון". וכי קאמינא דממון הוי להורישו לבניו, שאם יתבעוהו לאחר מיתת אביהן קנס שהיה חייב לאביהן, שהעמידו בדין ונתחייב, וכפר ונשבע והודה — הואיל וכשנפל ליורשין כבר היה ממון, שכבר עמד בדין ולא היה יכול להודות ולהפטר, א"כ הוי דומיא דפקדון דקרא ומחייב קרבן שבועה. איתיביה: "ר"ש אומר כו' דאחין הוא" — ופירוש: שאם אינו לאחין, איך מתחייב הכופר קרבן שבועה על טענותם? והא לאו בעל דברים דידהו הוא! אלא ש"מ דאחין הוא. ומסיק: כי קאמר רבה דממון הוא להורישו לבניו, בשאר קנסות לענין חיוב קרבן שבועה. ומסיק: דאצטריך "וכחש" לעמדה בדין ובגרה ואחר כך מתה — דמינה קא ירית, מכל מקום עיקרו קנס מיקרי לגבי דידה ודידיה, ולא דמי לשאר קנסות דמוריש לבניו דלגבי בניו לא הוה קנס כלל. ומיהו לשון "להורישו לבניו" לא משמע כפירוש זה. [ועיין תוספת בבא קמא עב. ד"ה סיפא]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:10:1.english: Is there [achievement of] grown-woman status in the grave, and it is her son's? - And if you say: How can [Rava] say that she bequeaths a fine to her son? Surely a person does not bequeath a fine to his children, as we say at the beginning of chapter Na'arah later (Ketubot 42b)! And shortly after as well, [the Gemara] says: "Is there grown-woman status in the grave, and the father's [right] ceases?" — and if a person bequeaths a fine, then even when there is grown-woman status in the grave, the father's [right] would not cease, and it would belong to him by right of inheritance [if she had no son]. However, that [proof from] shortly after can be deflected, as a practical difference arises if she owes money to others: for if there is grown-woman status in the grave, the father's [right] ceases — even though a person bequeaths a fine — so that the creditors collect [it]; whereas if there is no grown-woman status in the grave, the creditors do not collect anything, because the father's [right] does not cease and the fine is his and not hers. And one can say that here [too, the Gemara] could have asked: "Surely she does not bequeath a fine to her son!" Rather, it raises a stronger objection [instead]. And Ri establishes this dilemma here as referring to [the payments for] humiliation and impairment, which are [ordinary] monetary obligations and she can bequeath [them]. And even though we learned in the Mishnah at the beginning of Na'arah (Ketubot 41b): "[If] she did not manage to stand in court before the father died, they belong to herself" — and this refers to humiliation and impairment as well — from the fact that it teaches "they," it implies that [a father] cannot bequeath humiliation and impairment! And Ri says that regarding this matter, humiliation and impairment are certainly compared to the fine, as it is written: "because he afflicted her" (Deuteronomy 22:29), [from which we derive] by implication that there are [also] humiliation and impairment — [teaching] that to whomever this [the fine] is given, that [humiliation and impairment] is given; but for other matters they are not compared, for humiliation and impairment one pays on his own admission, whereas a fine one does not pay on his own admission. However, Rivam raised an objection: for we say in [chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 71b and there): [Rav Nachman] said to him: "Five oxen" (Exodus 21:37) the Merciful One stated, and not five halves of oxen. He raised an objection to him [from a baraita]: "If one stole from his father's [property] and slaughtered and sold [it], and afterward his father died, he pays the fourfold and fivefold payments." Now here, once his father died, he acquired his own portion [of the inheritance], and yet it teaches that he pays the fourfold and fivefold payments! And [the Gemara] answers: Here we are dealing with [a case] where he stood in court [before his father died]. This implies that were it not for "five oxen" and not five halves of oxen, it would work out well for him and he would not have needed to establish it as [a case] where he stood in court; thus, a person does bequeath a fine to his children! However, one can deflect [this proof], for he could have said "and according to your own reasoning." But [it is still] difficult, for [the Gemara] concludes: The next morning [Rav Nachman] said to him: "Five oxen" the Merciful One stated, and even five halves of oxen. [His interlocutor] said to him: What is the difference between the first clause and the latter clause? Explanation: for [the baraita] teaches [in the latter clause]: "If he stole from his father's [property] and [the father] died, and afterward he slaughtered and sold [it], he is exempt." [Rav Nachman] said to him: In the first clause, we apply to it "and he slaughtered it" entirely in [a state of] prohibition; in the latter clause, we do not apply "and he slaughtered it" entirely in [a state of] prohibition. This implies that where we apply to it "and he slaughtered it" entirely in [a state of] prohibition, he is liable even though he did not stand in court, because a person bequeaths a fine to his children — for if [it were] where he stood in court [prior to the father's death in the latter clause], he would not be liable for a fine, since he is slaughtering and selling his own! And Ri resolved that it speaks of [a case] where he stood in court [for the theft] and they said [to him]: "You are obligated to give [it] to him," so that if he slaughters [it] afterward he is liable, as we say in [chapter] HaGozel (ibid. 106b and there). And R. Yitzchak HaLavan resolved that that [passage] in chapter Na'arah deals with [the law] regarding an oath offering. And this is the explanation of that sugya there: I concede to you regarding an oath offering, for the Merciful One exempted him from "and he denied to his fellow regarding a deposit" (Leviticus 5:21). And when I say that it is a monetary obligation to bequeath it to his children, [it means] that if they claim from him after their father's death a fine that he owed their father — where he had already brought him to court and he was found liable, and he denied [it] and swore [falsely] and [later] confessed — since when it fell to the heirs it was already a monetary obligation, because he had already stood in court and could no longer confess and be exempt, therefore it is similar to a deposit [mentioned] in the verse, and he is liable for an oath offering. He raised an objection to him: "R. Shimon says, etc., that it belongs to the brothers" — and the explanation is: for if it does not belong to the brothers, how does the one who denies [it] become liable for an oath offering based on their claims? Surely he is not their litigant! Rather, learn from this that it belongs to the brothers. And [the Gemara] concludes: When Rabbah says that it is a monetary obligation to bequeath it to his children, [he says it] regarding other fines with respect to liability for an oath offering. And [the Gemara] concludes: that "and he denied" is needed for [a case where] she stood in court and became a grown woman and afterward died — for [even though her son] inherits from her, nevertheless its origin is called a fine with respect to her and him, and it is not comparable to other fines that one bequeaths to his children, where with respect to his children it was not a fine at all. However, the wording "to bequeath it to his children" does not sound like this explanation. [And see Tosafot on Bava Kamma 72a, s.v. seifa].

Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:1:1.hebrew: [אימא בתולה לג"ש - ולא נמעט בעולה, כדמשמע בסמוך. נראה דר"ע דריש ג"ש מקרא דלגופיה, דהיינו בתולה קמייתא ודקנס ודמפתה, אבל הבתולות דריש לכתובת בתולות, ולא שייך למידרשיה לג"ש ולא לשום רבוי. ואייתר נער, נערה, הנערה, וה' דהבתולות: חד לחייבי לאוין ועשה, וחד לחייבי לאוין וכריתות. ואיכא ג' רבויין — ה' דהבתולות, ונער, נערה, הנערה: חד לכדאביי, וחד לחייבי עשה, וחד לחייבי לאוין וכריתות. דאי איכא לר"ע חד לגופיה בלא ג"ש, א"כ נמעוט בעולה מההוא דלגופיה; ואף על גב דבקנס ליכא אלא חד בתולה דלגופיה, מגזירה שוה דמפתה ניליף בתולה ולא בעולה, כי היכי דיליף מפתה מאונס לענין נערה דלא כתיב במפתה]. (ת"י כ"י):
Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:1:1.english: [Say "virgin" is for a verbal analogy - and we would not exclude a non-virgin, as is implied shortly [in the Gemara]. It appears that Rabbi Akiva expounds the verbal analogy from a verse that is [also] needed for itself — namely, the first "virgin," and that of the fine [i.e., rape], and that of the seducer — whereas "the virgins" (ha-betulot) he expounds for the ketubah of virgins, and it is not applicable to expound it for a verbal analogy nor for any inclusion. And na'ar, na'arah, ha-na'arah, and the hei of ha-betulot are left over: one for those liable for negative commandments and a positive commandment, and one for those liable for negative commandments and karet. And there are three inclusions — the hei of ha-betulot, and na'ar, na'arah, ha-na'arah: one for that of Abaye, and one for those liable for a positive commandment, and one for those liable for negative commandments and karet. For if Rabbi Akiva had one [verse] for itself without the verbal analogy, then we would exclude a non-virgin from that [verse] which is for itself; and even though in [the passage of] the fine there is only one "virgin" which is for itself, from the verbal analogy of the seducer we would derive "a virgin" and not a non-virgin, just as the seducer [case] derives from rape with regard to "a young woman" (na'arah), which is not written in [the passage of] the seducer]. (Tosafot Yeshanim manuscript)

Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:1:2.hebrew: אימא בתולה לג"ש - תימה, דתיקשי ליה: דאימא תרוייהו לגופייהו ולא לג"ש! ונראה דהש"ס קים ליה דחד מינייהו לגזירה שוה, הואיל והמקראות סתומים לענין שקלים וחמשים, הלכך פריך: ואימא איפכא, ולא פריך: ואימא תרוייהו לגופייהו. וכי האי גוונא איכא פ"ק דסנהדרין (דף טז.), דאמר: ולא את נביא השקר אלא בב"ד של ע' ואחד; מה"מ? א"ר יוסי בר חנינא: אתיא "הזדה" "הזדה" מזקן ממרא. ופריך: הא "הזדה" כי כתיב בקטלא הוא דכתיב, וקטלא בכ"ג! אלא אמר ריש לקיש: גמר "דבר" "דבר" מהמראתו. והשתא, היכי הוה בעי למילף ולמימר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא דאתיא "הזדה" "הזדה"? אלא דהוה קים ליה דאיכא ג"ש, ולא הוה ידע במאי, וקאמר מסברא דאתיא "הזדה" "הזדה":
Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:1:2.english: Say [that the word] "virgin" [is] for a verbal analogy - It is astonishing, for [the Gemara] should have asked: Say [that] both of them [are needed] for themselves and not for a verbal analogy! And it seems that the Gemara was certain that one of them is for a verbal analogy, since the verses are unspecified regarding "shekels" and "fifty"; therefore, it asks: "And say the reverse," and does not ask: "And say both of them are for themselves." And a similar [case] to this is in the first chapter of Sanhedrin (16a), where it says: "[Nor do they judge] the false prophet except in a court of seventy-one." From where are these words [derived]? Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said: It is derived [via a verbal analogy of] "presumption" [and] "presumption" from a rebellious elder. And [the Gemara] objects: Behold, "presumption" — when it is written, it is written regarding execution, and execution is [judged] by twenty-three! Rather, Reish Lakish said: He derives [it via a verbal analogy of] "matter" [and] "matter" from his rebellion. Now, how could Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina have wanted to derive and say that it comes [from] "presumption" [and] "presumption"? Rather, he was certain that there is a verbal analogy, and did not know through which [word], so he said based on reasoning that it comes [from] "presumption" [and] "presumption."

Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:5:1.hebrew: מי אתיא גזרה שוה ומפקא ליה מפשטיה לגמרי - דדיוק הא אורסה הוי שקר. וקשה, דבריש הערל (יבמות ד' ע.) יליף דערל אסור בתרומה מגזירה שוה דתושב ושכיר מפסח, וכתיב: "תושב ושכיר לא יאכל בו" גבי פסח משום גזירה שוה, אע"פ שאינו אמת, דהא תושב ושכיר אוכלין בפסח כדאמרינן התם, דלא קני ליה רביה, ומפקי' קרא מפשטיה טפי מהכא! ואומר ר"ת, דההוא "תושב ושכיר" מיירי בערלים, ולהכי לא יאכל; ומוכח דלאו תושב ישראל קאמר, דהא לא קני ליה רביה, אלא ודאי בערל, ומשום הפנאה כתביה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:5:1.english: Does a verbal analogy come and divert it from its plain meaning entirely - For the inference "but [if she was] betrothed" is false. And this is difficult: for at the beginning of [the chapter] Ha'arel (Yevamot 70a), [the Gemara] derives that an uncircumcised person is forbidden [to eat] terumah from the verbal analogy of "sojourner and hired laborer" (toshav v'sachir) from [the laws of] the paschal offering; and it is written, "a sojourner and a hired laborer shall not eat of it" regarding the paschal offering [only] because of the verbal analogy, even though it is not literally true — for a sojourner and a hired laborer [may] eat of the paschal offering, as we say there, since his master does not acquire him — and [thus] we divert the verse from its plain meaning even more than here! And Rabbeinu Tam says that that [verse of] "sojourner and hired laborer" is speaking of uncircumcised people, and therefore he may not eat; and it is proven that it does not mean an Israelite sojourner, since his master does not acquire him, rather it certainly [speaks] of an uncircumcised person, and it wrote it for the sake of leaving it free [for the verbal analogy].

Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:6:1.hebrew: ארוסה בת סקילה היא - וא"ת: מאי קשיא ליה? הא השתא לא נפיק קרא ממשמעותיה, ואי לא איצטריך לגופיה, כ"ש דניחא טפי, דג"ש מופנה! ואומר ר"י דהכי פירושו: "ארוסה בת סקילה היא", וכיון דלא איצטריך למידי אלא לגזירה שוה, הוה ליה למכתב "אשר לא ארוסה" בהדיא; ואמאי שני למכתב "אשר לא אורסה", דאיכא למטעי ולמימר "הא אורסה" לעצמה? דבשלמא אי הוה בארוסה שום חידוש, הוה אתי שפיר במה ששינה הלשון, דאמרינן: האי דשנה וכתב "אורסה" — למדרש לגזירה שוה, ואתא פשטיה לחידושא. אבל השתא למה לי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:6:1.english: A betrothed woman is [subject to] stoning - And if you ask: What is the [Gemara's] difficulty? Behold, now [that Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak interprets it this way,] the verse does not depart from its plain meaning, and if it is not needed for itself, all the more so is it even better, since it is an unencumbered [mufneh] gezeirah shavah! And Rabbi Yitzchak says that this is its explanation: [The Gemara means:] "A betrothed woman is [subject to] stoning," and since [the verse] is not needed for anything except the gezeirah shavah, it should have written "who is not betrothed [arusah]" explicitly; why did it change [the wording] to write "who was not betrothed [orashah]," whereby one could err and say "but [if] she was betrothed [orashah]" on its own? For granted, if there were some novelty regarding a [currently] betrothed woman [arusah], it would work out well that it changed the wording, for we would say: the reason it changed and wrote "orashah" is to expound the gezeirah shavah, while its plain meaning comes for the novelty. But now, why do I need [that phrasing]?

Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:9:1.hebrew: לאבי הנערה ולא לאבי מתה - וא"ת: דבפרק נערה לקמן (כתובות דף מה:) גבי סרחה ולבסוף בגרה תידון בסקילה, דרשינן "הנערה" — שהיתה כבר. ויש לומר: דהתם מענינא דקרא, והכא מענינא דקרא; והתם ודאי אתיא לחייבה, דאי לפוטרה — לשתוק קרא מיניה, ואנא ידענא דלא הויא בסקילה, דלאו נערה היא. והכא, לחיובא דקנס לא אצטריך, דמסברא מיחייב אשעת ביאה, ואי אפשר לפוטרו בולא כלום; הלכך אתא לפוטרו:
Tosafot on Ketubot 38b:9:1.english: "To the father of the young woman," and not to the father of a dead [girl] - And if you ask: In the chapter [entitled] Na'arah below (Ketubot 45b), regarding [one who] sinned and subsequently became a bogeret [that] she is judged by stoning, we expound "the young woman" [to mean one] who was already [a young woman]. It can be answered that there [it is expounded] from the context of the verse, and here [it is expounded] from the context of the verse. There, [the verse] certainly comes to hold her liable, for if [it came] to exempt her, let the verse be silent about it, and I would know that she is not [subject] to stoning, since she is not a young woman. And here, [the verse] is not needed to obligate [him in] the fine, for by logical reasoning he is obligated at the time of intercourse, and it is impossible to exempt him for nothing; therefore, [the verse] comes to exempt him.
